headline: Hister offers fast, keyboard-based file search & full-text indexing
summary: This new tool aims to be a Linux equivalent to voidtool's Everything, with advanced features for local files and websites.
details: Hister is a new TUI-based tool designed for rapid file searching on Linux, inspired by voidtool's Everything but with a keyboard-centric interface. It allows users to define search zones and manage file history for quicker access.
Beyond file searching, Hister also functions as a full-text indexer for both local files and websites. It automatically saves visited pages, offering offline previews and a flexible search interface.

The project has seen an overwhelmingly positive initial reception, with over 30 contributors and hundreds of contributions. The developer aims to reduce reliance on traditional search engines like Google, DuckDuckGo, and Kagi by providing comprehensive local search capabilities.

The developer is also working on a separate project: a digital loyalty card system for cafes that integrates directly with Apple and Google Wallets without requiring any apps or customer sign-ups. This project is built using Ruby on Rails.

Additionally, the developer is involved in teaching kids visual scripting through a modified version of Overcooked 2, enabling them to code their way through game levels. This initiative is currently running an in-school pilot program.

headline_marked: [[AI is NOT taking over]] everything, says Hacker News
headline: AI is NOT taking over everything, says Hacker News
summary: A Hacker News discussion debunks the pervasive myth that AI is the sole driver of all technological advancement and usage.
details: A recent discussion on Hacker News highlights a growing sentiment that the pervasive narrative of AI dominating every aspect of technology is an oversimplification.
The conversation points out that while AI is significant, many other technologies and user needs continue to drive innovation and adoption.
Participants argue that focusing solely on AI overlooks crucial developments in areas like hardware, software infrastructure, and user experience design that are not directly AI-driven.
The consensus suggests a more balanced view is needed, acknowledging AI's impact without attributing every technological trend or user behavior to it.
caption:
Is AI really behind everything? A Hacker News discussion says no.

A recent discussion on Hacker News highlights a growing sentiment that the pervasive narrative of AI dominating every aspect of technology is an oversimplification.

The conversation points out that while AI is significant, many other technologies and user needs continue to drive innovation and adoption.

Participants argue that focusing solely on AI overlooks crucial developments in areas like hardware, software infrastructure, and user experience design that are not directly AI-driven.

The consensus suggests a more balanced view is needed, acknowledging AI's impact without attributing every technological trend or user behavior to it.
